Day 39 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Galaxy Collections

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished artifact recovered

Collections package modules, plugins, roles, playbooks and documentation so teams can reuse maintained automation instead of rebuilding every integration from scratch.

Architecture / mental model

requirements / Galaxy → collection install → fully-qualified module name → playbook

How it works

Collections are distributed bundles maintained by Ansible, vendors and the community. They extend the modules and plugins available to playbooks without copying implementation code into every repository.

The published example installed `amazon.aws` and then used a fully qualified module such as `amazon.aws.ec2_instance`.

Production use should make dependency versions deliberate. A collection is external code in your automation supply chain; pin and review it rather than assuming 'latest' is a stability strategy.

Hands-on reference

ansible-galaxy collection install amazon.aws
ansible-galaxy collection list
# Example module: amazon.aws.ec2_instance

Verification

List installed collections, run `ansible-doc` for the exact fully-qualified module and test the pinned collection version in a non-production target before fleet rollout.

Field note / gotcha

A collection name that works today can change behavior after an unpinned upgrade. Reuse saves work; dependency drift can quietly reintroduce it.

Security considerations

Review publisher/source, pin trusted versions, and treat collection updates like code dependency updates.

What I learned

Do not reinvent mature integrations, but do not outsource dependency control either.
